summary: Defines a Telnet option for determining the other module view of the status of options. It is an Internet Standard.

plainLanguage.summary: The Telnet Status option lets one end ask what option settings the other end believes are active. The reply reports the peer's view without changing those settings.

subtitle: Lets Telnet peers request and report their view of negotiated option settings.

tldr.problem: A Telnet process may need to check what option settings the other end believes are active without renegotiating those options.
tldr.mechanism: After permission is negotiated, one side can send STATUS SEND and the other can return STATUS IS containing its view of all option states.
tldr.outcome: The exchange reports a peer's view of current option status and avoids using renegotiation merely to discover that status.

today: RFC 859 is listed as an Internet Standard in the unit metadata. The metadata lists no RFC that updates or obsoletes it.

sections.title: Checking Telnet Option State
sections.content:
Telnet options such as echoing can be negotiated during a connection. Repeating those negotiations just to learn the current state can cause request loops.

The Status option lets one process check the other process's view of the current option settings through a separate status exchange.
sections.plainLanguage: A Telnet process may need to know which options are active at the other end. The Status option reports that view without renegotiating the options.

sections.title: Permission and Status Messages
sections.content:
WILL and DO are used only to agree that status information may be exchanged. After permission is established, the side that sent WILL STATUS can send status information, and the side that sent DO STATUS can request it.

A request uses IAC SB STATUS SEND IAC SE. A reply uses IAC SB STATUS IS, followed by the reported option states, and then IAC SE.
sections.plainLanguage: The peers first agree that they can exchange status. One side may then request a report, and the other sends its current view.

sections.title: Reading the Status Report
sections.content:
The IS report uses WILL, DO, and subnegotiation entries to describe option states. Options not explicitly listed are assumed to be in their default states, and one report describes all options.

The sender of WILL STATUS may also send a report without waiting for a request. At worst, both a spontaneous report and a requested report may be sent.
sections.plainLanguage: The report lists the options that are not in their default state. A peer can send a report on its own or after receiving a request.
